auditMethod: 5 parallel independent agent sessions, 2 companies each, separate from the agents that wrote the original reports; mined already-downloaded primary source files first, then web (KAP/MKK/IR/secondary) verification
constraints: no price targets or buy/sell recommendations produced
existing app BLOCKED/NEEDS_REVIEW decisions not changed
this audit itself is a single additional round, not independently re-reviewed by a third session

overallResult.strategicFitChanges: none — all 10 companies remain Kosullu Aday (B); none elevated to Cekirdek Aday (A), none downgraded to Uygun Degil (C), none D

TUPRS.evidenceReliability: bölüm bazlı: CFO=Yüksek, CAPEX=Düşük, temettü olgusu=Yüksek, temettü tam rakamları=Düşük-Orta; genel=Orta
keyFindings: CFO 2021-2025 series fully verified from primary source (y2021-y2025.txt), matches original report exactly
CAPEX 2021-2024 still unreliable — files were downloaded but PDF text extraction has column/row shift; not an access problem, a parsing problem
cyclicality numerically confirmed: CFO fell ~58-71% from 2023 to 2024 depending on calculation method
newRisksFound: normalized CFO (excluding 2022 super-cycle) ≈28bn TL/year, much lower than 2022-2023 peak capacity
unresolved: official dividend history PDF line-by-line verification

keyFindings: No primary financial statement PDFs were ever downloaded for FROTO in prior sessions (only price data) — the 'data not found' hypothesis for FROTO was NOT confirmed as 'already downloaded but unused'
Ford Otosan's own financial result PDFs are encrypted/compressed text streams, unreadable in this environment
correctedErrors: 24.03.2021 dividend was reported as '~13 TL, unverified'; actual verified figure from company IR page is 6.42 TL/share, total 2,252,842,200 TL (~2x smaller than prior estimate)
newRisksFound: third-party CFO/CAPEX series (investing.com) internally contradicts itself by ~24% (2024 CFO) and ~85% (2024 CAPEX) against other secondary sources
unresolved: payout ratio vs KAP profit distribution table

doas-fr2024-eng.pdf discovered to be a Cloudflare bot-protection HTML page, not a real PDF — previously unreadable, never flagged as such
correctedErrors: 2021-2023 CFO coverage ratios corrected downward significantly
2022 dividend amount discrepancy found (2.15bn claimed vs 1.935bn in primary cash flow statement, ~10% gap, unresolved)
newRisksFound: deterioration pattern now dated to at least 2022, not just FY2025

CNH Industrial's electrification roadmap (New Holland T4 Electric Power) confirmed as real and documented; TTRAK's own Turkey-specific response remains completely undocumented

FY2024 net debt magnitude (3 sources disagree)

~2.67bn TL gap between 8.5bn distributed and 5.825bn distributable base

AKSA.relativeRankingNote: among the stronger B companies by evidence quality
keyFindings: dividend table cross-checked line-by-line against Yahoo Finance with near-zero error — highest-confidence dividend data among the 10 companies
net debt/EBITDA 'irreconcilable' discrepancy (~2.8x company statement vs ~3.70x independent calc) resolved as a timing difference: 9A2026 figure is 2.84x
real/USD dividend growth absence independently confirmed via a second, CPI-independent method (direct USD comparison: $54.9M 2015 vs $50.5M 2025)
newRisksFound: parent-company net profit fell -24.5% YoY in 9A2026 even as EBITDA grew +43.6% and leverage improved — financing cost/FX effect still eroding profitability

AKMGY.relativeRankingNote: among the stronger B companies by cash-flow evidence quality, but with newly broader legal risk
keyFindings: the claim '2021-2025 CFO/CAPEX none verifiable from primary source' was REFUTED — a full 6-period primary CFO/CAPEX/FCF/payout series was produced from already-downloaded FY reports
payout-to-CFO ratio now calculable: FY2025 dividend paid exceeds CFO by 118.7%; FY2021 also exceeded CFO (122.1%)
newRisksFound: legal risk is broader than originally reported: at least 4 administrative lawsuits (2025/2596, 2025/2597, 2026/334, 2026/335) rejected at first instance, all on appeal — a second pair (2026/334-335) was not mentioned in the original report
share count (3,726,400,000) likely erroneous by ~100x based on strong indirect market-cap arithmetic; true figure likely ~37-55 million shares — unresolved, needs MKK confirmation
a 2026 gross dividend figure (14.21 TL) does not match the primary KAP filing (12.36 TL gross=net) — origin of the discrepancy unknown
unresolved: relationship between the 4th lawsuit and the 2025/2503 case

PAGYO.relativeRankingNote: among the stronger B companies on dividend continuity, but occupancy data quality downgraded
keyFindings: uninterrupted dividend history extended back to at least 2014 (12+ years, vs previously documented 10 years from 2016)
FY2021-2025 revenue/profit/CFO/CAPEX/FCF table spot-checked, no contradicting figures found
newRisksFound: occupancy rate inconsistency confirmed AND deepened: appraisal report says 91% ('current'), FY2025's own Note 6 sensitivity table says 97-98% (for both 2025 and 2024), FY2024's own Note 6 says 95-96% for 2024 — three documents disagree on the same year
small unresolved share count discrepancy: 87.0M declared vs ~89.4M implied by total cash dividend / per-share amount (~2.7% gap)

crossCuttingPatterns: TOASO, DOAS, TTRAK: independently discovered that dividends exceeded free cash flow in multiple past years, weakening the original 'disciplined history, recent/limited risk' framing in all three

YGGYO, PAGYO: both net-cash GYOs with legal minimum 50% distribution mandate, but both have deepened document-internal or cross-document numerical inconsistencies (YGGYO: FY2024 loss magnitude; PAGYO: occupancy rate) found this round

technical limitation across the board: no poppler/pdftoppm or equivalent PDF-to-image tool in this environment blocked visual verification of suspected PDF-text-extraction column/row shifts (TUPRS CAPEX, PAGYO Note 6 table)
